info.name: Cross_Border_Command - Full API (all 864 endpoints)
info.description:
Every route in `routes/api.php` (generated from `php artisan route:list` on 2026-10-30), grouped Module → Controller. Payloads are built from each controller's real `validate()` rules; every request's description lists the fields with required/optional and the full rule set.

**Start here:** set `login_email` / `login_password` in the environment, run `01 Auth & Account → Auth → POST /login`. Its test script stores `{{token}}` for every other call. If the email exists under several clients the response says `needs_org_selection`; resend with `client_id`.

**Conventions**
- All IDs in paths default to `1` - change them to rows that exist in your tenant.
- GET filters are listed as query params; optional ones are disabled (tick to send).
- `branch_id` on GETs mirrors the SPA branch switcher (disabled by default).
- Requests with files use form-data; PUT/PATCH with files are sent as POST + `_method`.
- Validation failures return 422 `{ message, errors }`.

request.description:
**AuthController@faceLogin**  
`POST /api/login/face`

**Auth:** PUBLIC (no token)
**Middleware:** `ThrottleRequests:20,1`

Face-based login. The SPA captures a face frame, computes the 128-d
descriptor with face-api.js and POSTs it here along with the user's
email. We compare against the enrolled descriptor on that user's
linked Employee row.

Threshold is tighter than attendance (0.50 vs 0.55) because this is
authentication — a false match here hands over the session. The face
is a SECOND factor in spirit, not the only factor: the user still
has to know which email account to identify themselves as.

All the same active-account / org / branch gates fire as the password
login, plus brute-force lockout on the same Cache key so an attacker
can't bypass rate-limiting by switching login methods.

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `email` | required | required / email |
| `descriptor` | required | required / array / size:128 |
| `descriptor.*` | required | required / numeric / between:-5,5 |
| `client_id` | optional | nullable / integer |

exec: else if (j.needs_org_selection) { console.log("Email exists in several clients - resend with client_id from", j); }

request.description:
**BranchController@shiftOptions**  
`GET|HEAD /api/branch-shifts`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Work-shift options for the Employee form's Shift dropdown.

Resolves the branch the same way employee creation does:
 - branch_user  → their own branch's shifts
 - client_admin → the branch the BranchSwitcher points at (?branch_id);
   with "All Branches" selected there is no single branch, so we return
   the union of every branch's shifts (deduped by name).
 - super_admin  → the requested branch_id.

Response: { shifts: [{ name, start, end }, ...] }. Empty when nothing is
configured — the frontend then falls back to its default list.

**MasterController@counts**  
`GET|HEAD /api/master-counts`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Batch count endpoint for the Master dashboard. Returns a `{ slug:
{ active, inactive, total } }` map covering every registered master
the current user has `can_view` on. The dashboard previously made one
/master/{slug} request per card (~50 round-trips); this collapses
everything into a single query so the Active/Inactive pills paint
within a single tick, regardless of which masters are in the menu.

Perm-denied or empty tables fall back to {active:0, inactive:0, total:0}
so the card never gets stuck in its "loading" state.

request.description:
**MasterController@bulk**  
`GET|HEAD /api/master/bulk`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

GET /api/master/bulk?keys=departments,designations,roles&fields=id,name

Several master lists in one response.

The Employee screen opened with ten separate master fetches, each a full
round trip, serialised behind the browser's connection limit — 2.3s to
6.6s on the wire for about 30 KB of data that changes maybe monthly. The
payload was never the problem; the request count was.

Each key is served by list() itself rather than a re-implementation, so a
change to scoping, permissions or the ?fields trim applies to both paths
automatically. A key the caller may not see is omitted rather than
failing the whole call — one forbidden master should not blank nine
legitimate ones.

**ConsigneeController@destroy**  
`DELETE /api/consignees/{consignee}`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

**ConsigneeController@cloneFromCustomer**  
`POST /api/consignees/{consignee}/clone-from-customer`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

"Same as Customer" deep-clone. Copies the linked customer's Stage 2
KYC documents (Company DD + Trade Licence) and Owner KYC rows onto
this consignee — including their file attachments via
Storage::copy(). The consignee's *additional addresses* are already
carried in the consignee POST/PUT payload, so this endpoint only
handles the children that live in separate tables.

Replace semantics: each call wipes the consignee's existing KYC
(rows + on-disk files) and re-clones fresh from the customer. This
keeps "Same as Customer" semantically truthful — re-ticking and
re-saving always produces an exact mirror, even if the customer's
KYC was edited after the consignee was first created. Manual edits
on the consignee side are intentionally overwritten; the user
opted into that by re-ticking the box.

Tenant scope: both ends are checked. Customer must be visible to
the caller via Customer::forUser($user), same as the
cross-tenant guard used by store/update.

Route: POST /api/consignees/{id}/clone-from-customer
Body:  { "customer_id": <int> }

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | required | required / integer / exists:customers,id |

**ConsigneeController@mapCustomer**  
`POST /api/consignees/{consignee}/map-customer`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Map an EXISTING consignee to a customer (many-to-many). Used by the
customer's "Add Or Map Consignee → Map" flow. Attaches the pivot row
(idempotent) and merges the customer's segment(s) into the consignee's
segment list when the customer carries a segment the consignee lacks.

Body:  { "customer_id": <int> }

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `customer_id` | required | required / integer / exists:customers,id |

request.description:
**CustomerController@gstAvailable**  
`GET|HEAD /api/customers/gst-available`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Live "is this GSTIN free?" check for the Add/Edit Customer form.

Purely a UX affordance — it tells the user a number is taken BEFORE
they fill the rest of the form. It is NOT the guard: two users can
pass this check in the same second and both submit, so the closure
rule in validatePayload() is what actually enforces uniqueness.

Scope: client + branch, resolved from the authenticated user via
resolveOwnership() so it matches store()/update() exactly (a GSTIN may
legitimately repeat across branches, but not within one). Never trust a
client_id/branch_id from the request.

Returns the holder's name so the UI can say WHO has it — deliberately
limited to the caller's own branch, so nothing leaks across tenants.

request.description:
**VendorController@productMappings**  
`GET|HEAD /api/vendors/{id}/product-mappings`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Read-only product mappings for ONE supplier — powers the "Mapped
Products" popup opened from the count badge on the supplier list.

index() already ships `product_mappings_count` for the badge itself;
this fills the popup once it's clicked. GET /vendors/{id} would answer
the same question, but it eager-loads the ~16 relations the 3-step
wizard needs (documents, owners, bank accounts, GST scrutiny, segment
uploads) — far too much for a 9-column read-only table, and it doesn't
even carry HSN / segment (the wizard backfills those client-side from a
separate 500-row /products fetch). Joining them here means the popup is
one small request with nothing to reconcile afterwards.

Scoped through the same forUser() visibility rule as index(), so a
supplier outside the caller's tenant 404s rather than leaking rows.

request.description:
**ClmAgreementController@libraryShow**  
`GET|HEAD /api/clm/agreement-library/{id}`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

One agreement, with its document body — what the editor opens.

Scoped exactly as libraryIndex() scopes the list, NOT as libraryUpdate()
scopes an edit. Those differ: the list passes the requested branch filter
while an edit is pinned to the caller's own branch. Scoping this like an
edit meant a row the user could see in the list came back 404 when they
opened it. Whatever the list showed, this serves; whether it may then be
SAVED is still libraryUpdate's decision.

**ClmSegmentRuleController@forSegment**  
`GET|HEAD /api/clm/segment-rules/for-segment/{segmentId}`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

GET /clm/segment-rules/for-segment/{segmentId}

Resolve the segment-rule for a given segment plus the FULL document
master rows referenced by its doc_selections payload, so the consumer
forms (AddCustomer, AddConsignee, AddVendor) can pre-populate their
Stage-2 KYC / DD / Trade-Document lists without three extra fetches.

Response shape — always 200 even when no rule exists, so the caller
can render an empty Stage 2 instead of having to swallow a 404:
  {
    "rule": null | { … },
    "kyc": [ { code, name, authority, requirement: 'M'|'O', … } ],
    "dd":  [ … ],
    "tl":  [ … ],
    "qc":  [ … ]
  }

The same shape as CtcContractController::previewLive, and it renders the
same blade the real download does — that is the whole point: a preview
built from a different view would agree with the editor and disagree
with the file people actually receive.

posts its current content, margins, header and footer on every debounce,
so the preview tracks unsaved edits. The row is looked up only to give
the blade a title and a code, and only inside the caller's own tenant.

paints it with pdf.js.

it back same-origin with a `Content-Disposition: attachment` header, so
the download works everywhere. Tenant-scoped: the path must belong to a

GET /api/segment-uploads/{type}/{id}/vault

Compose the Evidence Vault payload. Combines three sources:
  1. The entity's segment(s)              → which rules apply
  2. Each rule's doc_selections           → expected documents
  3. segment_doc_uploads for the entity   → what's actually attached

Returned shape mirrors VaultData on the frontend so the modal
plugs in without further mapping:
  {
    total_documents, verified_signed, pending,
    company_dd_count, owner_kyc_count, trade_license_count,
    trade_documents_count, total_shipments,
    company_dd: [{id,name,reference,authority,issue_date,expiry,attachment,attachment_url,status}, …],
    owner_kyc: […], trade_licenses: […], trade_documents: […],
    shipment_agreements: [],
    last_updated
  }

Status semantics:
  • An uploaded doc      → 'Verified'
  • A doc the rule wants → 'Pending' (no upload yet)
  • The shipment_agreements bucket is intentionally empty until
    the per-shipment compliance matrix lands as its own table.

**AnnouncementController@attachment**  
`GET|HEAD /api/announcements/{id}/attachment`

**Auth:** PUBLIC (no token)
**Middleware:** `ValidateSignature`
**Signed URL:** needs the `expires` + `signature` query string from the emailed link.

PUBLIC (signed) — stream a broadcast announcement's attachment.

The emailed announcement links here instead of a raw /storage or Azure
blob URL, so the link opens on BOTH local and Azure (public or private
container) and works even when the recipient isn't logged in. The route
carries a `signed` signature so the id can't be tampered with. Streamed
inline so PDFs/images open in the browser (still downloadable from there).

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

"Is this email free?" — asked by Stage 1 of the employee wizard before it
tries to save, so the duplicate is reported on the field the operator is
standing on rather than after a round trip through the rest of the form.

The answer is SYSTEM-WIDE (#221): an address held anywhere in this
database, by any client, in any branch, by a login, an employee, a
candidate, an organisation contact or a trade party, is taken. Nothing is
disclosed about who holds it — EmailGuard::message names the KIND of
record and never the record, because the holder may sit in a tenant this
user cannot see.

**EmployeeController@updateBankDetails**  
`PUT /api/employees/{id}/bank-details`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Self-service / HR update of an employee's bank & payment details only.

The full update() requires master.employees can_edit, which an ordinary
employee never holds — so once bank details were captured at onboarding,
nobody could correct them afterwards (#35: "no one can edit the bank
details"). This narrow endpoint lets the employee fix their OWN payout
account, while HR / branch users (holding can_edit) can fix anyone's in
their tenant. Only the bank columns are written — pay, status and every
other field are left untouched.

**EmployeeController@forceDestroy**  
`DELETE /api/employees/{id}/force`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Permanently delete a soft-deleted employee. Only callable on a row
already in the Disabled tab — we refuse to force-delete an active
employee outright to prevent accidental data loss from a single
misclick on the wrong tab.

The paired login user is NOT hard-deleted: it gets locked to
inactive and its tokens revoked, but the row stays so permissions
+ activity_logs + audit trails that reference user_id don't go
dangling. Only the Employee row itself is removed for good.

**EmployeeController@updateStep**  
`PATCH /api/employees/{id}/step`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

PATCH /employees/{id}/step — the wizard's master-data save.

Same validation as the full update: validatePayload() is the method
store() and update() both call, so the rules cannot drift apart. Every
rule is nullable on an update and validated() returns only the keys that
were sent, so a partial body is checked exactly as the same keys would
be through PUT.

What it does NOT do is the reason it exists — no fullWith() eager load,
no dependent-column re-derivation, no rebuilt employee in the response.
Measured against the same two-master-id save: 36 queries through update(),
under ten here.

A key outside STEP_SAFE_FIELDS is refused with 422 and `fallback: true`,
which is the caller's signal to send the same body to PUT /employees/{id}.
Refusing is deliberate: silently ignoring an unsafe field would write
half a save and skip the side effect that field exists to trigger.

**LeaveRequestController@sandwichWaiver**  
`POST /api/leave-requests/{id}/sandwich-waiver`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Set or clear the Sandwich Leave Policy waiver on a single leave, and
re-size `days` to match.

Recomputing here is the whole point. `days` is the one number both the
leave balance and the payslip read, so a waiver that only changed a flag
would leave the employee's balance down 4 while payroll paid 2, with
nothing to reconcile the two. Flipping the flag and re-deriving `days` in
the same transaction keeps them a single fact.

Reachable from the leave approval screen and from the payroll run screen;
both write here rather than each keeping their own idea of the waiver.

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `waived` | required | required / boolean |
| `reason` | optional | nullable / string / max:255 |

**ExpenseClaimController@exportPdf**  
`POST /api/expense-claims/export-pdf`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Render the on-screen Expense / Advance export as a real PDF. (#166)

"Export ▸ PDF" used to open a print window and call window.print(), so the
user got a print dialog and had to know to choose "Save as PDF" — the
report was never actually exported, and a pop-up blocker stopped it
outright. Every other PDF in this app is produced server-side with dompdf
and streamed back as a download; this brings the expense export in line.

The already-formatted headers/rows come FROM the screen rather than being
re-queried here, deliberately: the export must contain exactly what the
user is looking at, and the module toggle, status tab, date range and
search box are all client-side state. Re-deriving that server-side would
be a second implementation of the same filtering, free to disagree with
the first. The Blade escapes every cell, so nothing in the payload can
reach the document as markup.

| `title` | required | required / string / max:200 |

| `rows` | required | present / array / max:5000 |

**ExpenseClaimController@setDeductions**  
`POST /api/expense-claims/{id}/set-deductions`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

POST /expense-claims/{id}/set-deductions
Lock the ONE-TIME deduction on an approved claim WITHOUT recording a payment.
Computes the sanctioned amount (claim − Σ deductions) and freezes it so every
later payment pays against a fixed net-payable. Can only run before the first
payment (i.e. while the sanctioned amount is still unset).

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `deductions` | optional | nullable / array |
| `deductions.*.amount` | required | required_with:deductions / numeric / min:0 |

| `additions` | optional | nullable / array |
| `additions.*.amount` | required | required_with:additions / numeric / min:0 / max:100000 |
| `additions.*.reason` | optional | nullable / string / max:500 |

**ExpenseClaimController@settle**

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

POST /expense-claims/{id}/settle
Record ONE settlement installment against an approved claim. The FIRST call
also sets the sanctioned amount (+ deduction reason when it's less than the
claim). Partial payments are allowed until the sanctioned amount is met.

      amount, category_id?, payment_type, expense_type, note.

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `deductions` | optional | nullable / array |

| `additions` | optional | nullable / array |

**RecruitmentController@linkedHiringRequests**

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Ids of the hiring requests that have already become a recruitment.

The Hiring Requests modal needs exactly this set — to split its rows
into Pending / Recruitment Created and to decide whether "Create
Recruitment" is offered. It used to get it by fetching the ENTIRE
recruitments list, with every eager-loaded relation attached, and

to build a Set of numbers.

Deliberately not folded into stats(): that endpoint is narrowed by
?search so its badges agree with the rows on screen, whereas this set
classifies hiring requests and must cover the whole tenant regardless of
what anyone has typed. Same reason it does not take a status filter — a
cancelled recruitment still means that request was converted.

`GET|HEAD /api/recruitments/stats`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

KPI tiles + tab badges for the Recruitment list.

Separate from index() for the reason every paginated list needs it: the
browser used to count these off the full array, which only worked while
index() returned every row. Once the list answers one page, counting it
reports "Total Recruitments 10" on a tenant of 50.

Narrowed by ?search but NOT by ?status — the badges are the breakdown
the status tabs are cut FROM, so filtering them by the active tab would
leave every tab reading its own count and zero for the others. Search is
applied so the badges agree with the rows underneath them; a search that
narrowed the table but left the tabs at their full totals is a screen
contradicting itself.

request.description:
**ExitController@fnfSummary**  
`GET|HEAD /api/employees/{employee}/exit/fnf-summary`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Everything owed to, or recoverable from, this employee at exit — the
inputs to the Full & Final settlement, pulled from the modules that
actually hold them instead of being retyped by HR.

  GET /api/employees/{employee}/exit/fnf-summary

A leaver is dropped from the regular payroll run for their exit month
(PayrollService::eligibleEmployees excludes anyone whose last working day
falls in the cycle), so the salary they earned up to that day is one of
the lines here — otherwise it would never be paid at all.

Read-only. Nothing is written; the exit stage decides what to carry over.

**ExitController@reassignReports**  
`POST /api/employees/{employee}/exit/reassign-reports`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Move direct reports onto a new reporting manager.

Accepts one assignment per employee, so the SPA can do a bulk "everyone to
this manager" or individual picks with the same call. Every assignment is
re-validated here: the SPA greys out ineligible options, but the rules
that matter (tenant scope, seniority, self-reference, not the person being
exited) are enforced on this side too.

All-or-nothing — a partial reassignment would leave the org chart in a
state neither the operator nor the closure gate can reason about.

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `assignments` | required | required / array / min:1 |
| `assignments.*.employee_id` | required | required / integer / exists:employees,id |
| `assignments.*.reporting_manager_id` | optional | nullable / integer / exists:employees,id |
| `assignments.*.reporting_manager_user_id` | optional | nullable / integer / exists:users,id |

**ExitController@rehire**  
`POST /api/employees/{employee}/rehire`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Rehire an exited employee — bring them back as active staff.

  POST /api/employees/{employee}/rehire
  { "restart_onboarding": bool, "note": string|null }

Only a STANDARD RESIGNATION can be rehired here. Someone who walked out
without serving notice, or who was terminated, is not re-activated with
one click: that decision needs a fresh hiring process, and a blacklisted
leaver must not come back at all. The SPA greys the button for those
cases; this is the server-side twin so a direct call can't bypass it.

The exit row is kept and stamped `rehired_at` rather than deleted — the
exit is history worth having, and every "is this person exited?" reader
treats a stamped row as spent.

`restart_onboarding` sends them back through onboarding so HR can refresh
bank details, address and documents; otherwise the login is simply
switched back on with the record as it stood.

| Field | Required | Rules |
|---|---|---|
| `restart_onboarding` | optional | nullable / boolean |
| `note` | optional | nullable / string / max:500 |
| `rejoining_date` | optional | nullable / date / 'after_or_equal:' . now()->toDateString() / 'before_or_equal:' . now()->addYears(2)->toDateString() |

**HrDocumentSignatureController@previewSigners**  
`GET|HEAD /api/hr-document-signatures/preview-signers`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Who WOULD sign, and under what job title, if this template were sent for
this employee now. Read-only: nothing is created or written.

The signing workflow stored on a template names ROLES ("Employee",
"Reporting Manager", "Client (CEO)") and almost never a designation —
designation_name is null on every template in practice. Until a run
exists there is no person and no job title to show, so the stepper could
only print the bare role, which is what "designations are missing when
sending for signature" reports (#23).

Resolution is the SAME SignerResolver::resolve() that store() uses, so
the preview cannot drift from what the send actually does. It stays a
preview, though: store() resolves again at send time on purpose, so that
a re-org between looking and sending is reflected rather than frozen
from whatever was on screen.

**HrDocumentSignatureController@downloadSignedPdf**  
`GET|HEAD /api/hr-document-signatures/{id}/download-pdf`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

PDF version of the signed document.

A COMPLETED run is rendered ONCE and the file kept (signed_pdf_path);
every later download streams it. Two reasons, and the first is the one
that matters:

  Evidence. Re-rendering from content_html plus the signature image
  files means the copy handed over a year later is only as stable as
  those files and as this renderer. A stored PDF is what was signed.

  Speed. A render is seconds — DomPDF, plus a blob fetch per inlined
  image; measured 4.2s per download on production. A file read is not.

An in-flight run is never stored, because it still gains signatures, so
it renders on demand as before.

**HrDocumentSignatureController@remind**  
`POST /api/hr-document-signatures/{id}/remind`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Send a reminder email to the CURRENT pending signer on an
in-flight workflow. HR uses this when a signer has been sitting
on a doc — instead of pinging them on chat, click Reminder and
the system emails them a polite nudge with the document link.

Behaviour:
 - Only fires on Pending / In Progress runs (Completed / Rejected
   / Cancelled don't have a "current signer" to remind).
 - Only emails the signer whose turn it is (sequential mode);
   the rest are still waiting their turn and shouldn't get
   reminders yet.
 - Audit-logs the reminder so the admin can see how many nudges
   have been sent from the Audit Trail timeline.
 - Throttles to once per 6 hours per signer to avoid spam if HR
   clicks the button repeatedly.

**PayrollController@sandwichReview**  
`GET|HEAD /api/payroll/sandwich-review`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

Leaves inside the selected cycle whose day count the branch's Sandwich
Leave Policy has inflated — the review list the payroll screen shows so a
genuine emergency can be excused before the run is finalised.

The policy fires on the shape of the calendar and cannot tell a
bereavement from a stretched long weekend. Payroll is the last point at
which a human sees the consequence in money terms, so the exemption has
to be reachable from here — not only from the leave approval screen the
approver saw weeks earlier.

Read-only. Toggling the waiver itself goes through
LeaveRequestController::sandwichWaiver(), which also re-sizes the leave,

request.description:
**PurchaseOrderDocumentController@evidenceVault**  
`GET|HEAD /api/p2p/orders/{po}/evidence-vault`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

GET /p2p/orders/{po}/evidence-vault — every document filed against this
order, including each invoice raised under it.

The same service the invoice's own vault uses, entered from the other
end: the order and its trade documents, then a block per SPI carrying
that invoice, its e-way bill, a sticker per box and the packing images,
then every payment proof released — each naming the invoice it answered.

Read-only, and separate from index() on purpose: that one owns the PO's
document ROWS and the Necessary marking, while this gathers paperwork
from four tables and writes nothing.

**SpiPutawayTaskController@activity**  
`GET|HEAD /api/putaway/tasks/{task}/activity`

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

GET /putaway/tasks/{task}/activity — what happened, in order.

The task row says WHERE it ended up; this says how it got there, and it
is the only place the REFUSALS survive. A put-away that took four
attempts and one wrong rack reads identically to a clean one on the task
row alone — the difference lives here, and it is the difference worth
reading when someone asks why a box took twenty minutes.

**Auth:** Bearer token (`auth:sanctum` → `user.active` → tenant context)

GET /inventory/racks/{rack}/shelves/next-code

A shelf code is not built from the shelf's own id — it is
RC-003-SH-02, the RACK's code plus the shelf's level within it. So the
next code is the next LEVEL in this rack, not the next sequence value,
and unlike the other three it is contiguous: levels are counted, not
handed out, so a deleted shelf's level is reused by the next one.

Still a preview — two people adding a shelf to the same rack are both
shown this, and the second will get the level after.

request.description:
**DevToolsController@mailPreview**  
`GET|HEAD /api/dev/mail-preview/{template}`

**Auth:** PUBLIC (no token)

GET /dev/mail-preview/{template} — render a transactional email as a web
page, for checking the design.

Renders the blade and returns it. Nothing is sent, nothing is queued and
no mail transport is touched, so it answers on a machine with no SMTP
configured and leaves no row in the jobs table.

LOCAL ONLY. It takes its sample data from the query string, so on a live
host it would let anyone render a branded message with text of their
choosing — a ready-made phishing page on your own domain. Hence the 404
rather than a 403: outside local the route does not exist.
